items.title: Official Baseball Rules, 2026 Edition
items.summary: The current code of playing rules governing MLB and the professional development leagues. Nine numbered rule groups (1.00-9.00), a Definitions of Terms glossary and appendices with field/strike-zone diagrams.

structured_payload.publisher: Office of the Commissioner of Baseball

items.title: Rule 1.00 — Objectives of the Game
items.summary: Baseball is a game between two teams of nine players under a manager, played on an enclosed field under umpires. The offense tries to have batters become runners and advance; the defense tries to prevent that. A run scores when a runner legally touches all bases, and the team with more runs at the end of a regulation game wins.

items.title: Rule 2.00 — The Playing Field
items.summary: Specifies field layout and mandatory dimensions: a 90-foot infield square, home-to-second of 127 feet 3 3/8 inches, a pitcher's plate 60 feet 6 inches from home and 10 inches above it, minimum fence distances, a 95-foot infield grass-line radius, and the size of home plate, the bases and the pitcher's plate.

key_points: 325/400 ft for fields built after June 1, 1958

items.title: Rule 3.00 — Equipment and Uniforms
items.summary: Governs the ball, the bat, uniforms, catcher's mitt, first baseman's glove, fielding gloves, pitcher's glove, helmets, undue commercialization and equipment on the field. It sets maximum bat dimensions and glove sizes and restricts the pitcher's glove colour.

key_points: pitcher's glove may not be white or gray

items.title: Rule 4.00 — Game Preliminaries
items.summary: Covers umpire duties before the game, the manager, the exchange of lineup cards (including how to handle a player not listed on the card), weather and field conditions, special ground rules, fraternization, security and doubleheaders.

items.title: Rule 5.00 — Playing the Game
items.summary: The core playing rules: starting the game, fielding positions, base coaches, batting and the batting order, when the batter becomes a runner, running the bases, pitching mechanics and violations, scoring, making an out, appeal plays, substitutions and pitching changes including mound visits and the three-batter minimum, the designated hitter and dead balls.

items.title: Rule 6.00 — Improper Play, Illegal Action and Misconduct
aliases: 6.00 Improper Play, Illegal Action and Misconduct
Improper Play, Illegal Action and Misconduct
items.summary: Defines interference (offensive, defensive, umpire, spectator), obstruction, catcher collisions, the fielder right of way, pitcher illegal actions including balks and illegal pitches, batter illegal actions including batting out of turn, and unsportsmanlike conduct.

structured_payload.rule_title: Improper Play, Illegal Action and Misconduct

items.title: Rule 7.00 — Ending the Game
items.summary: Defines regulation games, suspended games, forfeited games and protested games, including when a game becomes official and how play is terminated.

items.title: Rule 8.00 — The Umpire
items.summary: Covers umpire qualifications and authority, appeal of umpire decisions, umpire positioning, reporting, and the General Instructions to Umpires.

items.title: Rule 9.00 — The Official Scorer
items.summary: The official scoring rules: scorer duties and reports, runs batted in, base hits and their value, stolen bases and caught stealing, sacrifices, putouts, assists, double and triple plays, errors, wild pitches and passed balls, walks, strikeouts, earned runs, winning and losing pitchers, shutouts, saves, statistics, percentage records and minimum standards for championships.

items.title: Rule 1.01 — Objectives
items.summary: Baseball is a game between two teams of nine players each under a manager, played on an enclosed field under one or more umpires.

items.title: Rule 1.02 — Offensive objective
items.summary: The offensive team's objective is to have its batter become a runner and its runners advance.

items.title: Rule 1.03 — Defensive objective
items.summary: The defensive team's objective is to prevent offensive players from becoming runners and to prevent their advance.

items.title: Rule 1.04 — Scoring a run
items.summary: A batter who becomes a runner and legally touches all bases scores one run.

items.title: Rule 1.05 — Winning objective
items.summary: Each team's objective is to win by scoring more runs than the opponent.

items.title: Rule 1.06 — Winner
items.summary: The team that has scored more runs at the conclusion of a regulation game wins.

items.title: Rule 2.01 — Layout of the field
items.summary: The infield is a 90-foot square; the pitcher's plate is 10 inches above home plate; minimum distance requirements apply to fences and stands, with stricter minima for fields constructed after June 1, 1958.

items.title: Rule 2.02 — Home base
items.summary: Home base is a five-sided slab of whitened rubber, a 17-inch square with two corners removed, set with its point at the intersection of the first and third base lines.

items.title: Rule 2.03 — The bases
items.summary: First, second and third bases are 18-inch square bags between three and five inches thick, filled with soft material.

items.title: Rule 2.04 — The pitcher's plate
items.summary: The pitcher's plate is a 24-inch by 6-inch slab set so the distance from the plate to the rear point of home plate is 60 feet 6 inches.

items.title: Rule 2.05 — Benches
items.summary: The home club furnishes roofed benches for both teams, not less than 25 feet from the base lines.

items.title: Rule 3.01 — The ball
items.summary: Specifies the weight, circumference and construction of the official ball.

items.title: Rule 3.02 — The bat
items.summary: The bat must be a smooth round stick; MLB bats are solid wood with a maximum length of 42 inches and maximum diameter of 2.61 inches at the thickest part.

items.title: Rule 3.03 — Player uniforms
items.summary: Every player on a team must wear a uniform of the same colour, style and pattern, with no ragged or distracting elements.

items.title: Rule 3.04 — Catcher's mitt
items.summary: Specifies the dimensions and padding of the catcher's mitt.

items.title: Rule 3.05 — First baseman's glove
items.summary: Specifies the dimensions of the first baseman's glove, which may be a mitt or a glove.

items.title: Rule 3.06 — Fielding gloves
items.summary: Fielding gloves are limited in size (maximum 12 inches from top to heel) and in the width of the web.

items.title: Rule 3.07 — Pitcher's glove
items.summary: The pitcher's glove may not be white or gray, nor may it have a colour that distracts the batter.

items.title: Rule 3.08 — Helmets
items.summary: Batters, runners and catcher's headgear must meet the prescribed protective requirements.

items.title: Rule 3.09 — Undue commercialization
items.summary: Uniforms and equipment may not carry undue commercialization.

items.title: Rule 3.10 — Equipment on the field
items.summary: Only permitted equipment may be on the playing field.

items.title: Rule 4.01 — Umpire duties
items.summary: Umpires have pre-game duties including field inspection and receiving the lineup cards.

items.title: Rule 4.02 — Field manager
items.summary: The manager represents the team in communications with umpires and is responsible for the club's conduct.

items.title: Rule 4.03 — Exchange of lineup cards
items.summary: The manager delivers the batting order to the umpire, who gives a copy to the opposing manager; the rule also addresses a player not listed on the lineup card.

items.title: Rule 4.04 — Weather and field conditions
items.summary: The home manager decides whether to start or continue a game because of weather or field conditions, subject to the umpire-in-chief's authority.

items.title: Rule 4.05 — Special ground rules
items.summary: The home club may establish special ground rules for its park, which must be approved by the umpire-in-chief and communicated to both teams.

items.title: Rule 4.06 — No fraternization
items.summary: Players and coaches may not fraternize with the opposing team during a game.

items.title: Rule 4.07 — Security
items.summary: The home club must provide adequate security and keep the field and stands orderly.

items.title: Rule 4.08 — Doubleheaders
items.summary: A doubleheader consists of two games played in immediate succession, with rules for when one is scheduled or rescheduled.

items.title: Rule 5.01 — Starting the game
items.summary: The umpire-in-chief calls 'Play Ball!' to start the game; the visiting team bats first unless otherwise agreed.

items.title: Rule 5.02 — Fielding positions
items.summary: Defines the nine fielding positions and the pitcher's legal position (windup and set).

items.title: Rule 5.03 — Base coaches
items.summary: Two base coaches may be stationed in the coach's boxes; the 2026 edition adds penalties for a coach who does not stay within the box.

items.title: Rule 5.04 — Batting
items.summary: Covers the batting order (each player bats in turn), the batter's box (the batter must stay within it), and completing a time at bat. Includes the three-official check-swing guidance.

items.title: Rule 5.05 — When the batter becomes a runner
aliases: 5.05 When the batter becomes a runner
When the batter becomes a runner
items.summary: A batter becomes a runner on a fair hit, a walk, a hit-by-pitch, catcher's interference and other specified events, with base awards.

structured_payload.rule_title: When the batter becomes a runner

items.title: Rule 5.06 — Running the bases
items.summary: How runners occupy and advance bases, when they must retouch, and which balls are dead; the 2026 edition clarifies the retouch responsibility.

items.title: Rule 5.07 — Pitching
items.summary: Legal pitching deliveries from the windup and set positions, warm-up pitches, pitcher delays, throwing to bases, removing the pivot foot and ambidextrous pitchers.

items.title: Rule 5.08 — How a team scores
items.summary: A run scores when a runner legally advances to and touches home plate before the third out, subject to exceptions such as a force out or a batter-runner retired before reaching first.

items.title: Rule 5.09 — Making an out
items.summary: Retiring the batter, retiring a runner, appeal plays, the effect of a preceding runner's failure to touch a base, and retiring the side.

items.title: Rule 5.10 — Substitutions and pitching changes
items.summary: Substitution rules, including visits to the mound, the three-batter minimum for relievers, and improper substitutions.

items.title: Rule 5.11 — Designated hitter rule
items.summary: The designated hitter bats in place of the pitcher; the rule governs the DH's role and what happens if the DH enters the field.

items.title: Rule 5.12 — Calling time and dead balls
items.summary: When the umpire calls 'Time' and when the ball becomes dead, and the resulting base awards.

items.title: Rule 6.01 — Interference, obstruction and catcher collisions
items.summary: Defines batter/runner interference, fielder right of way, catcher interference, unintentional interference, spectator interference, coach and umpire interference, interference with a squeeze play or steal of home, obstruction, collisions at home plate and sliding on double-play attempts.

items.title: Rule 6.02 — Pitcher illegal action
items.summary: Balks, illegal pitches with bases unoccupied, and pitching prohibitions (such as a quick pitch or applying a foreign substance).

items.title: Rule 6.03 — Batter illegal action
items.summary: When a batter is out for an illegal action, and the batting-out-of-turn rule and its remedies.

items.title: Rule 6.04 — Unsportsmanlike conduct
items.summary: Prohibits unsporting acts and sets warnings, ejections and discipline.

items.title: Rule 7.01 — Regulation games
items.summary: A game is regulation once the losing team has had five turns at bat (or 4.5 innings with the home team ahead); the 2026 edition clarifies Commissioner authority to terminate play.

items.title: Rule 7.02 — Suspended games
items.summary: A suspended game is resumed from the point of suspension under specified conditions.

items.title: Rule 7.03 — Forfeited games
items.summary: A game may be forfeited for specified rule violations, with a 9-0 score recorded.

items.title: Rule 7.04 — Protesting games
items.summary: A manager may protest a game for a rule misinterpretation; the protest is decided by the league office.

items.title: Rule 8.01 — Umpire qualifications and authority
items.summary: Umpires must be qualified and have authority to enforce the rules and maintain order.

items.title: Rule 8.02 — Appeal of umpire decisions
items.summary: How a manager may appeal an umpire's decision, including arguing only on a rule interpretation, and the consequences of excessive argument.

items.title: Rule 8.03 — Umpire position
items.summary: Specifies standard umpire positions with and without runners on base.

items.title: Rule 8.04 — Reporting
items.summary: Umpires report ejections and incidents to the league office.

items.title: Rule 9.01 — Official scorer (general rules)
items.summary: The official scorer records the game, makes judgment calls on hits and errors, and may not be a member of either club.

items.title: Rule 9.02 — Official scorer report
items.summary: The scorer's report and the information it must contain.

items.title: Rule 9.03 — Official scorer report (additional rules)
items.summary: Additional reporting requirements and corrections.

items.title: Rule 9.04 — Runs batted in
items.summary: An RBI is credited for a run driven in by a base hit, sacrifice, groundout, force out or similar; not for a run scored on an error or a double play in specified cases.

items.title: Rule 9.05 — Base hits
items.summary: A base hit is credited when a batter reaches base safely on a fair ball that is not handled by a fielder, subject to the ordinary-effort standard.

items.title: Rule 9.06 — Determining value of base hits
items.summary: Classifies hits as one-base, two-base, three-base or home run, and governs scoring when a fielder mishandles the ball.

items.title: Rule 9.07 — Stolen bases and caught stealing
items.summary: Credits a stolen base when a runner advances on a pitch without a hit, out, error or other specified cause, and a caught stealing when put out.

items.title: Rule 9.08 — Sacrifices
items.summary: A sacrifice bunt advances a runner and puts the batter out; a sacrifice fly scores a runner. Neither counts as an at-bat.

items.title: Rule 9.09 — Putouts
items.summary: A putout is credited to the fielder who catches a fly ball or tags or forces a runner.

items.title: Rule 9.10 — Assists
items.summary: An assist is credited to a fielder who throws or deflects the ball in a way that leads to a putout.

items.title: Rule 9.11 — Double and triple plays
items.summary: Credits a double play when two offensive players are put out by continuous action without an error between putouts, and a triple play for three.

items.title: Rule 9.12 — Errors
items.summary: An error is charged when a fielder misplays a ball that an ordinary-effort fielder would have handled, allowing a runner to advance.

items.title: Rule 9.13 — Wild pitches and passed balls
items.summary: A wild pitch is charged to the pitcher for a pitch too high, low or wide to be handled; a passed ball is charged to the catcher for a pitch the catcher should have handled.

items.title: Rule 9.14 — Base on balls
items.summary: A walk is credited when a batter receives four pitches outside the strike zone; an intentional walk may be signalled without pitching.

items.title: Rule 9.15 — Strikeouts
items.summary: A strikeout is credited to the pitcher for a third strike, whether swinging, looking or on a foul bunt.

items.title: Rule 9.16 — Earned runs and runs allowed
items.summary: An earned run is one that scores without the aid of an error or passed ball; the rule reconstructs the inning to determine earned runs.

items.title: Rule 9.17 — Winning and losing pitcher
items.summary: Sets how the winning and losing pitchers are determined, including the starter's five-inning requirement.

items.title: Rule 9.18 — Shutouts
items.summary: A shutout is credited when a pitcher pitches a complete game without allowing a run.

items.title: Rule 9.19 — Saves for relief pitchers
items.summary: A save is credited to a finishing reliever who protects a lead under the specified criteria.

items.title: Rule 9.20 — Statistics
items.summary: General requirements for compiling and reporting official statistics.

items.title: Rule 9.21 — Determining percentage records
items.summary: How batting, fielding, pitching and winning percentages are computed.

items.title: Rule 9.22 — Minimum standards for individual championships
items.summary: Minimum plate appearances, innings pitched and games played required to qualify for season championships; typically 3.1 plate appearances per team game and 1 inning pitched per team game.

items.title: Rule 9.23 — Guidelines for cumulative performance records
items.summary: Guidelines for cumulative records and how plays are recorded.

items.title: Balk
items.summary: An illegal act by the pitcher with one or more runners on base; all runners advance one base. It is a delayed dead ball unless the pitcher's illegal act is also a pitch that the batter hits and all runners advance at least one base.

structured_payload.definition: An illegal act by the pitcher with one or more runners on base; all runners advance one base. It is a delayed dead ball unless the pitcher's illegal act is also a pitch that the batter hits and all runners advance at least one base.
conditions: at least one runner on base
an illegal act by the pitcher during a delivery or while on the rubber
exceptions: if the batter reaches first and all runners advance at least one base, the balk is ignored
common_misconceptions: a balk is not automatically called when a pitcher merely fakes a throw; the specific act matters
a balk requires runners; with no runners, some violations become an illegal pitch instead

items.title: Infield Fly
items.summary: A fair fly ball (not a line drive or bunt) that can be caught by an infielder with ordinary effort when first and second, or first, second and third, are occupied with fewer than two out. The batter is out and the ball remains live; runners may advance at their own risk.

structured_payload.definition: A fair fly ball (not a line drive or bunt) that can be caught by an infielder with ordinary effort when first and second, or first, second and third, are occupied with fewer than two out. The batter is out and the ball remains live; runners may advance at their own risk.
conditions: fair fly ball
ordinary effort by an infielder
first and second occupied (or bases loaded)
fewer than two outs
exceptions: a bunt or a line drive is never an infield fly
common_misconceptions: the infield fly is not triggered by the fielder's position alone; it is about ordinary effort
the ball stays live; runners are not automatically awarded bases

items.title: Dropped Third Strike
items.summary: When strike three is not caught by the catcher, the batter may attempt to reach first base, unless first base is occupied with fewer than two out or the batter was put out by the third strike. The pitcher still receives credit for the strikeout.

structured_payload.definition: When strike three is not caught by the catcher, the batter may attempt to reach first base, unless first base is occupied with fewer than two out or the batter was put out by the third strike. The pitcher still receives credit for the strikeout.
conditions: third strike not caught cleanly
first base unoccupied or two outs
exceptions: first base occupied with fewer than two outs: the batter is out immediately
common_misconceptions: the batter may run only when the third strike is not caught; a caught third strike ends the at-bat
the pitcher is credited with a strikeout even if the batter reaches base

items.title: Force Play
items.summary: A play in which a runner legally loses the right to occupy a base because the batter becomes a runner. The force is removed when the batter-runner is put out or a preceding runner is retired.

structured_payload.definition: A play in which a runner legally loses the right to occupy a base because the batter becomes a runner. The force is removed when the batter-runner is put out or a preceding runner is retired.
conditions: a runner is forced to advance because the batter becomes a runner
exceptions: the force is removed once the batter-runner is put out or the following runner is retired on the play
common_misconceptions: a force out is not the same as a tag out; once the force is removed the runner must be tagged
runs can score before a tag out after the force is removed

items.title: Tag Play
items.summary: A play in which a fielder retires a runner by touching the runner with the ball securely held in the fielder's hand or glove. A tag is also used to retire a runner who is not forced.

structured_payload.definition: A play in which a fielder retires a runner by touching the runner with the ball securely held in the fielder's hand or glove. A tag is also used to retire a runner who is not forced.
conditions: the fielder has secure possession of the ball and touches the runner
exceptions: a forced runner may be retired by touching the base instead of tagging
common_misconceptions: a fielder does not need to tag the base on a tag play
the ball must be held after the tag

items.title: Appeal Play
items.summary: A play in which a team asks the umpire to rule on a violation that is not automatically called, such as a runner failing to touch a base or leaving too soon on a caught fly. The appeal must be made before the next pitch or play.

structured_payload.definition: A play in which a team asks the umpire to rule on a violation that is not automatically called, such as a runner failing to touch a base or leaving too soon on a caught fly. The appeal must be made before the next pitch or play.
conditions: the defending team appeals before the next pitch, play or attempted play
exceptions: an appeal may be made by tagging the runner or the base, depending on the violation
common_misconceptions: umpires do not call these violations on their own; the defense must appeal
a runner is not automatically out for missing a base unless appealed

items.title: Interference
items.summary: An act that illegally impedes a fielder's attempt to make a play. Offensive interference is by the team at bat; defensive interference (catcher's interference) hinders the batter; umpire and spectator interference are also defined. Penalties depend on the type.

structured_payload.definition: An act that illegally impedes a fielder's attempt to make a play. Offensive interference is by the team at bat; defensive interference (catcher's interference) hinders the batter; umpire and spectator interference are also defined. Penalties depend on the type.
conditions: the act hinders, impedes or confuses a fielder or batter
exceptions: contact that is incidental to a legitimate play is not necessarily interference
common_misconceptions: interference and obstruction are different: interference is by the offense or spectator, obstruction by a fielder without the ball
a runner need not intend to interfere

items.title: Obstruction
items.summary: The act of a fielder who, while not in possession of the ball and not in the act of fielding it, impedes the progress of any runner. The penalty is a delayed dead ball and the umpire awards bases to nullify the obstruction.

structured_payload.definition: The act of a fielder who, while not in possession of the ball and not in the act of fielding it, impedes the progress of any runner. The penalty is a delayed dead ball and the umpire awards bases to nullify the obstruction.
conditions: a fielder without the ball impedes a runner
exceptions: a fielder in the act of fielding the ball is not obstructing
common_misconceptions: obstruction is not called only for contact; impeding the runner's path is enough
the ball is usually delayed dead, not immediately dead

items.title: Fielder Right of Way
items.summary: Fielders have the right of way on a batted ball they are attempting to field; a runner who interferes with a fielder making a play may be called out.

structured_payload.definition: Fielders have the right of way on a batted ball they are attempting to field; a runner who interferes with a fielder making a play may be called out.

items.title: Catcher's Interference
items.summary: Defensive interference by the catcher that hinders or prevents the batter from hitting a pitch. The batter is awarded first base and other runners advance if forced, unless the batter reaches base and the offense prefers the play.

structured_payload.definition: Defensive interference by the catcher that hinders or prevents the batter from hitting a pitch. The batter is awarded first base and other runners advance if forced, unless the batter reaches base and the offense prefers the play.
conditions: the catcher hinders the batter's swing or contact
exceptions: the offense may decline the award if the play is more advantageous
common_misconceptions: catcher's interference is a form of defensive interference
it awards first base even on a swing

items.title: Spectator Interference
items.summary: Interference by a spectator (or an object thrown by a spectator) that hinders a player's attempt to make a play on a live ball. The 2026 edition clarifies its application to batted, thrown or pitched balls.

structured_payload.definition: Interference by a spectator (or an object thrown by a spectator) that hinders a player's attempt to make a play on a live ball. The 2026 edition clarifies its application to batted, thrown or pitched balls.

items.title: Collisions at Home Plate
items.summary: A runner may not deviate from the path to initiate contact with the catcher; the catcher without the ball may not block the runner's path to the plate. The 2026 edition clarifies appropriate set-up positions for catchers without the ball.

structured_payload.definition: A runner may not deviate from the path to initiate contact with the catcher; the catcher without the ball may not block the runner's path to the plate. The 2026 edition clarifies appropriate set-up positions for catchers without the ball.

items.title: Sliding to Bases on Double-Play Attempts
items.summary: A runner sliding into a base on a double-play attempt must make a bona fide effort to reach the base and may not make contact above the knee or with a rolling block. Interference may be called and the double play completed.

structured_payload.definition: A runner sliding into a base on a double-play attempt must make a bona fide effort to reach the base and may not make contact above the knee or with a rolling block. Interference may be called and the double play completed.

items.title: Foul Ball
items.summary: A batted ball that settles on foul territory between home and first or third, bounds past first or third base on or over foul territory, first falls on foul territory beyond first or third, or while on or over foul territory touches an umpire, player or foreign object. A foul fly is judged by the ball's position relative to the foul line.

structured_payload.definition: A batted ball that settles on foul territory between home and first or third, bounds past first or third base on or over foul territory, first falls on foul territory beyond first or third, or while on or over foul territory touches an umpire, player or foreign object. A foul fly is judged by the ball's position relative to the foul line.
common_misconceptions: a ball that lands fair and rolls foul past the base is a fair ball
the fielder's position does not determine fair/foul

items.title: Fair Ball
items.summary: A batted ball that settles on fair ground between home and first or third, is on or over fair territory when bounding past first or third, touches first/second/third base, first falls on fair territory on or beyond first or third, or passes out of the playing field in flight over fair territory.

structured_payload.definition: A batted ball that settles on fair ground between home and first or third, is on or over fair territory when bounding past first or third, touches first/second/third base, first falls on fair territory on or beyond first or third, or passes out of the playing field in flight over fair territory.

items.title: Catch
items.summary: The act of a fielder securing possession of a ball in flight in the hand or glove and holding it firmly, without using the cap, protector, pocket or uniform. It is not a catch if the fielder collides with a player or wall or falls and drops the ball, or if the ball strikes a runner or umpire before another fielder catches it.

structured_payload.definition: The act of a fielder securing possession of a ball in flight in the hand or glove and holding it firmly, without using the cap, protector, pocket or uniform. It is not a catch if the fielder collides with a player or wall or falls and drops the ball, or if the ball strikes a runner or umpire before another fielder catches it.
conditions: secure possession
the ball is in flight
the fielder holds it after contact with the ground or a wall
exceptions: a ball held only briefly and dropped on transfer is not a catch in some scoring contexts
common_misconceptions: a catch requires control long enough to prove the fielder has the ball, not a fixed number of steps
a fielder who goes to the ground must hold the ball after landing

items.title: Check Swing
items.summary: A batter's attempt to stop a swing. The plate umpire may ask a base umpire for help; the appeal is to the base umpire's judgment of whether the batter struck at the pitch. Rule 5.04 provides guidance for the official check-swing review.

structured_payload.definition: A batter's attempt to stop a swing. The plate umpire may ask a base umpire for help; the appeal is to the base umpire's judgment of whether the batter struck at the pitch. Rule 5.04 provides guidance for the official check-swing review.

items.title: Dead Ball
items.summary: A ball out of play because of a legally created temporary suspension of play. Runners may not advance, be put out or score while the ball is dead, and the umpire calls 'Time'.

structured_payload.definition: A ball out of play because of a legally created temporary suspension of play. Runners may not advance, be put out or score while the ball is dead, and the umpire calls 'Time'.
common_misconceptions: a dead ball is not the same as a foul ball; fouls are one cause of a dead ball

items.title: Live Ball
items.summary: A ball in play when the umpire has not called 'Time'. Runners may advance and be put out, and runs may score.

structured_payload.definition: A ball in play when the umpire has not called 'Time'. Runners may advance and be put out, and runs may score.

items.title: Base Award
items.summary: The number of bases the umpire awards to runners and the batter when the ball goes out of play or when a play is nullified. Awards are generally one, two, three or four bases depending on the situation.

structured_payload.definition: The number of bases the umpire awards to runners and the batter when the ball goes out of play or when a play is nullified. Awards are generally one, two, three or four bases depending on the situation.

items.title: Runner Abandonment
items.summary: A runner who abandons the base path and does not attempt to advance or return may be called out when the ball is put back in play and the defense appeals.

structured_payload.definition: A runner who abandons the base path and does not attempt to advance or return may be called out when the ball is put back in play and the defense appeals.

items.title: Batting Out of Turn
items.summary: When a player bats out of order, the opposing manager may appeal; the proper batter is out and the intervening action may be nullified depending on when the appeal is made.

structured_payload.definition: When a player bats out of order, the opposing manager may appeal; the proper batter is out and the intervening action may be nullified depending on when the appeal is made.
conditions: the defense appeals before the improper batter's turn is completed and before a pitch to the next batter
exceptions: if the improper batter reaches base and no appeal is made before the next pitch, the improper batter becomes the proper batter
common_misconceptions: umpires do not call batting out of turn automatically; the defense must appeal
the wrong batter is not always the one called out; the proper batter is

items.title: Designated Hitter
items.summary: A player who bats in place of the pitcher without playing a position. The DH is a starting player; if the DH enters the field to play defense, the team loses the DH and the pitcher must bat in that lineup spot.

structured_payload.definition: A player who bats in place of the pitcher without playing a position. The DH is a starting player; if the DH enters the field to play defense, the team loses the DH and the pitcher must bat in that lineup spot.
conditions: the DH is listed on the lineup card and bats for the pitcher
exceptions: a two-way player may be designated differently under league rules
common_misconceptions: the DH and the pitcher are not separate lineup slots once the DH is removed

items.title: Pitch Timer
